name: Number theory: the hidden life of whole numbers
description: Divisors, primes, remainders, congruences and codes, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Number theory realm ("Number theory: the hidden life of whole numbers"): divisors, primes, congruences, powers and codes, for an
adult who has finished Foundations and Discrete mathematics. Same Kepler outpost, now with a Signal Office and a cipher room, where
Mira locks the outpost's messages. The concept plan is docs/plans/NUMBER-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Divisors and primes
chapters.blurb: Remainders, bases, primes, factorisation, gcd, lcm and Euclid’s algorithm.

sector.name: Crate Store
sector.purpose: pack every delivery into equal crates with nothing left over

chapters.name: Combining whole numbers
chapters.blurb: Bézout’s coefficients, whole-number equations and counting and adding divisors.

sector.name: Fuel Depot
sector.purpose: measure out exact amounts with only the cans we have

chapters.name: Congruences
chapters.blurb: Working mod n, divisibility tests, inverses and linear congruences.

sector.name: Timetable Office
sector.purpose: run every timetable on its own repeating cycle

chapters.name: Powers and remainders
chapters.blurb: The Chinese remainder theorem, fast powers, Fermat, φ and Euler.

sector.name: Signal Office
sector.purpose: send huge numbers through a small channel

chapters.name: Special numbers and orders
chapters.blurb: Wilson’s theorem, Möbius, perfect numbers, orders and primitive roots.

sector.name: Calendar Hall
sector.purpose: line up cycles of every length on the Kepler year

chapters.name: Squares and primes
chapters.blurb: Quadratic residues, the Legendre symbol, reciprocity, sums of squares and testing primes.

sector.name: Survey Field
sector.purpose: lay out plots whose sides are whole numbers

chapters.name: Fractions and secret codes
chapters.blurb: Continued fractions, best approximations and RSA.

sector.name: Cipher Room
sector.purpose: send messages only the outpost can read

copy.homeTitle:
Whole numbers keep secrets.
Learn to read them.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Signal Office. Every crate count, timetable and coded message here rests on how whole numbers divide. We start by packing one delivery into equal crates.
copy.allDone: The outpost’s codes are now yours to make and to break. Graph theory opens next in the Map Room, where numbers become networks.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from divisors to codes. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the answer before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Read whole numbers closely.
help.intro: Number theory starts where Discrete maths ends: with divisors, remainders and counting. It asks how whole numbers divide, repeat and hide one another, and uses those facts to pack crates, time timetables and send codes. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Residues are typed as least residues from 0 to n − 1, a Legendre or Möbius value as −1, 0 or 1, and a yes or no as 1 or 0; any answer of 1000 or more is typed without commas.
